one_liner: A 52-year-old right-handed female with progressive worsening of vision, dysarthria, headache, and incoordination following a motor vehicle accident experienced progressive neurological decline and was discharged to a care facility.

procedures.outcome: Revealed atypical mononuclear cells suggestive of tumor or reactive lymphocytosis

procedures.outcome: Noted variable caliber in the RMCA, LACA and Left AICA distributions

procedures.outcome: Inconclusive, showed atypical mononuclear cells and lymphocytes

course.narrative: A 52-year-old female experienced progressive neurological symptoms including vision changes, dysarthria, headache, and incoordination following a motor vehicle accident. Extensive workup including multiple lumbar punctures, brain MRIs, a cerebral angiogram, and a temporal artery biopsy showed persistent T2 signal abnormalities in the brainstem, cerebellar peduncles, and temporal lobes, suggesting glioma or vasculopathy. She received a short course of IV steroids. A left temporal lobe brain biopsy showed atypical mononuclear cells and lymphocytes that were ultimately considered reactive. Her neurological state progressively worsened throughout her hospital stay, requiring NGT feeding and 24-hour supportive care. She was made DNR at family request and transferred to a care facility.

disposition.condition: very somnolent and difficult to arouse
